summary:
BEYOND EARTH

BEYOND EARTH is an interactive 3D space exploration and mission simulation game designed to make space science more accessible, engaging, and educational. Our project allows players to experience the challenges of space missions, from selecting launch sites, rockets, spacecraft, and crews to exploring the Moon and Mars.

The game integrates real-world weather data from Open-Meteo and daily solar radiation data from NASA POWER to support informed launch-site decisions. Inspired by NASA research, including Artemis, VIPER, and MOXIE, the simulation introduces players to rocket physics, orbital mechanics, resource management, and planetary exploration.

Players must make critical decisions, respond to spacecraft emergencies, operate rovers, extract water from Martian ice, produce oxygen, and develop sustainable habitats.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming complex scientific concepts into an interactive learning experience that connects NASA research with practical problem-solving.

BEYOND EARTH is important because it encourages STE(A)M education, critical thinking, creativity, and teamwork while inspiring the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.
details: BEYOND EARTH is an interactive 3D space exploration and mission simulation game designed to make space science more engaging, accessible, and educational. Players can select launch sites, rockets, spacecraft, and astronaut crews, analyze real-world weather conditions, manage essential resources, and experience space missions involving rocket launches, spacecraft emergencies, lunar exploration, and Mars colonization. The game includes scientific challenges such as extracting water from Martian ice, producing oxygen, growing food, operating rovers, and maintaining astronaut survival systems. We developed our project using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Python, Bootstrap, and Three.js, with Visual Studio Code (VS Code) as our primary development environment. We also used browser developer tools for testing and debugging, the Open-Meteo API for current weather information, and the NASA POWER API for daily solar radiation data. NASA research, including the Artemis, VIPER, and MOXIE projects, provided scientific inspiration for our missions. Our team focused on scientific accuracy, educational value, user-friendly controls, 3D visualization, accessibility, performance, and sustainability. What makes BEYOND EARTH creative is its combination of real environmental data, interactive simulations, strategic decision-making, and interconnected survival systems within a single educational game. Instead of simply watching space missions, players actively solve problems and experience the consequences of their decisions. Our goal is to strengthen STEM education, encourage critical thinking and teamwork, and inspire young people to explore science, engineering, and space technology. Ultimately, we aim to make learning about space exploration an exciting, meaningful, and interactive experience for students around the world.
